narrative.overview:
The site is a darkroom: near-black ground, amber light as atmosphere, photographs presented as wet prints with fibre-paper borders. Chrome stays subordinate to the print. Brand and enquire are the only bright signals that compete with the image; everything else reads as room, tray, or caption.

Personality is unhurried and material. Density is sparse — one composition in the first viewport, then a staggered run of prints, then short copy. The world refuses the category-default dark-minimal name-over-grid portfolio: no equal card grids, no eyebrow kickers, no glass marketing panels.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground with safelight amber as atmospheric pools, never as an image tint
Fibre-paper cream for print borders and the sole bright Enquire control
Bricolage Grotesque for brand and UI; Literata for leads, body, and captions
Trays and stacked prior prints as depth — not cards
Sharp UI corners; soft drop shadows only under trays and prior sheets

rules.name: The Safelight Rule
rules.body: Amber is light in the room, not a brand wash. Use it for pools, selection, and thin accents; never tint photographs or flood backgrounds.

rules.name: The Fibre Paper Rule
rules.body: Cream is the print edge and the Enquire signal. It is scarce on purpose — if cream appears as a large page field, the darkroom has failed.

rules.name: The Quiet Chrome Rule
rules.body: On any screen, the photograph outranks navigation, labels, and supporting copy. If chrome competes with the print, remove chrome.

rules.name: The Brand-Is-Display Rule
rules.body: The photographer’s name is the display size. Do not place a larger marketing headline above or beside it.

rules.name: The Serif-For-Voice Rule
rules.body: Literata carries sentences and captions; Bricolage carries names, section titles, nav, and buttons. Do not invert the pairing.

rules.name: The One Composition Rule
rules.body: The first viewport holds brand, one lead, one CTA group, one dominant tray print, and atmospheric room (safelight + prior stack). No stats, schedules, or secondary marketing in that frame.

rules.name: The Staggered Print Rule
rules.body: Portfolio prints alternate left/right on a single track. Never a same-size card grid of photographs.

rules.name: The Tray-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: Photographs sit in recessed trays with fibre borders. Do not wrap images in bordered, radius, or equal-height cards.

rules.name: The Soft Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft black drops under material objects (trays, sheets). No hard offset neobrutalist shadows; no decorative multi-layer glows on chrome.

rules.name: The Square Bench Rule
rules.body: Interactive chrome is sharp-cornered. Roundness belongs only to light pools.

dos: Do keep the photographer’s name as the hero display signal and the dominant brand mark.
Do present photographs as fibre-bordered trays on near-black ground with soft tray shadows.
Do reserve safelight amber for atmospheric pools, selection, and thin accents.
Do use fibre-paper cream for print borders and Enquire — scarcity is the signal.
Do pair Bricolage for brand/UI with Literata for captions and body voice.
Do stagger prints left/right on a single track with generous vertical gap.
donts: Don't build a dark-minimal name-over-equal-image-grid portfolio.
Don't introduce cards, eyebrow kickers, pill clusters, or stat strips.
Don't tint photographs with amber or flood the page with cream.
Don't use hard offset shadows, multi-layer chrome glows, or rounded-full controls.
Don't let supporting copy or nav outrank the print in the first viewport.
Don't invent review scores, prices, or booking calendars — the sample stays honest and quiet.
